description:
FOUND s484c (Opus, 2026-09-14) by #1719's probe row 14.  PRE-EXISTING and
independent of #1719's advance rule.

perl sets the match variables from the LAST match an s///g made; PCL sets them
from the FIRST.  Probed 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl (scratch/s484c/probe/p1719-b.pl
row 14):

    my $z = 'a1b22c'; $z =~ s/(\d+)/-/g; print $1;
        perl 22        PCL 1

CAUSE, located: `do-regex-subst`'s NON-EVAL arm (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) runs one
`cl-ppcre:scan` of its own BEFORE the replacement, purely to set $1../$&, and
that scan finds the first match; the loop that follows (regex-replace-all with
a string replacement) sets nothing.  The /e arm beside it is RIGHT by
construction -- its per-match lambda calls set-capture-groups/set-match-vars
for every match, so the last call wins (probed: the same row with s///ge
answers 22 in PCL too, which is the discriminating measurement).

FIX SHAPE (untried): the non-eval /g arm must set the match variables from the
LAST match, not the first.  %p-global-scanner (s484c) already sees every match
the loop takes, so the cheapest shape is for it to keep the last match's
offsets and register vectors and for the arm to call the two setters once after
the loop -- which also DELETES the up-front scan, so the subject is scanned
once instead of twice.  A no-match s///g must still leave the variables alone
(perl does), which the "only if the loop matched" guard gives for free.

Note the non-global s/// arm has the same up-front scan and is CORRECT there
(one match, so first = last); leave it.

BAR: the row above plus a /e twin (already right, must stay right), $&, $`, $',
@-, @+ after an s///g with 2+ matches, a no-match s///g leaving a previous
match's variables intact, and the `while (/(\d+)/g)` m//g loop (the m// path
already sets per match).  A `cl/` change, so the full sweep plus the re/ + op/
companion legs.


=== EVIDENCE (s491, Fable, 2026-09-19; main 4c6565e5) ===
The same up-front scan owns MORE than $1: after a non-/e `s///g` AND after `s///gr`, `@-`, `@+`, the prematch and the postmatch are the FIRST match's (perl: the LAST).  Probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/p-subst-matchvars.pl (+ .perl.out / .main-4c6565e5.out): `my $h = "aXbXc"; $h =~ s/X/-/g;` -> perl `[@-]=[3] [@+]=[4] prematch aXb postmatch c`, PCL `[1] [2] a bXc`; the `/ge` arm (row 5) and list-context `m//g` (row 4) are RIGHT, so only the non-eval arm diverges.  PERF NOTE for #1808 (s473x was told): the up-front scan is one EXTRA scan per substitution -- a replace loop that records the match it is on (no allocation per match: overwrite ONE record) removes that scan AND closes this task, which is the cheap shape if #1808 goes to shape 1.
subject: after s///g perl's $1 is the LAST match's capture and PCL's is the FIRST -- do-regex-subst's non-eval arm sets the match variables from an up-front scan it makes before the loop
